faq.q: What are good holiday party games for adults?
faq.a: The ones that take a sentence to explain and work in teams: white elephant, team trivia, name that tune, minute to win it, charades, fishbowl and a photo scavenger hunt. For big crowds, heads or tails and a left-right gift pass get everyone playing at once. Pick three for one party: a mixer, a main event and a closer.

faq.q: What games can you play at an office holiday party?
faq.a: White elephant, team trivia with an “our year” round, name that tune with winter songs, minute to win it, a photo scavenger hunt, guess the baby photo, a desk-decor swap and a gingerbread build-off. Keep every game optional, non-religious and sober, and avoid anything that puts one person on the spot.

faq.q: How do you play white elephant?
faq.a: Everyone brings one wrapped gift under a set price and draws a number. Player one opens a gift. Each next player either opens a new gift or steals an opened one, and anyone who loses a gift opens a new one or steals a different one. A common house rule freezes a gift after its third steal. Allow about two minutes per player.

faq.q: What are good holiday games for large groups?
faq.a: Choose games where everyone plays at once. Heads or tails takes five minutes and one coin for any crowd size. A left-right gift pass works at every table, find-someone-who bingo gets people mingling, and a Family Feud-style game built from a survey of your guests works on a stage with two teams.

faq.q: How many games should you plan for a holiday party?
faq.a: Three is the sweet spot: a mixer as people arrive, a main event after food, and a quick closer before people leave. Give each one 15 to 30 minutes. A background game like a shared camera or bingo card can run all night alongside them without needing any extra time.
